# Playbook for Win As Much As You Can

When I see the payoff matrix, I need to map out what each outcome means: understand that picking X when others pick Y gives me a big advantage, but if everyone picks X, we all break even. This is a prisoner's dilemma.

When opponents pledge Y in a talk phase, I should pledge Y as well, not X. Going for individual advantage early signals that I can't be trusted, which invites retaliation in later high-multiplier rounds. The structure of this game rewards coordination more than I initially recognized.

When I pick Y while others pledge and pick Y, we maintain mutual trust and build toward the high-multiplier rounds where cooperation yields the largest absolute gains for everyone.

When the multiplier on an upcoming round is high (x5 or x10), that round matters most. I should prioritize maintaining cooperation through those rounds rather than exploiting a short-term advantage earlier.

Perfect cooperation maintained throughout the game—matching all opponents' pledges and picks of Y from round 1 through round 10—keeps all players tied and maximizes total welfare. This episode shows that sustained coordination works: we each finished at +25, which is better than any individual could achieve by defecting.

When opponents pledge Y consistently and honor those pledges with Y picks, trust is real. Continue picking Y to preserve it. Do not assume they will defect later just because the multiplier is high; if they've been reliable, they likely will continue to be.

When facing the final round with a high multiplier, do not defect. If trust is intact, we all benefit more from mutual Y than from any individual exploitation. A tie at maximum points beats a hollow first-place finish after others retaliate.

When all players remain perfectly tied throughout, the game becomes about whether we can all coordinate to maximize collective and individual outcomes. We did this successfully.

When trust has held through every round including all high-multiplier rounds (x3, x5, x10), and all opponents continue pledging Y in the final talk phase, defecting in round 10 would break trust for a single round's gain. By that point the pattern is established: they will pick Y. Staying with Y secures the best outcome for everyone and confirms that coordination was the winning strategy all along.

Next time: pledge Y when they pledge Y. Pick Y when they pick Y, especially before and during high-multiplier rounds. Maintain cooperation consistently from start to finish. If they have cooperated reliably through every high-multiplier round and pledged Y again before the final round, do not break faith in the last moment. Coordination in this game beats exploitation, and a tied maximum outcome is preferable to a fractured game where defection and retaliation lower everyone's final score.

WIN AS MUCH AS YOU CAN -- you, Ash, Beck and Coda; 10 rounds.
Each round every player simultaneously picks X or Y. Payoffs depend on how many picked X:
  1 X: the X gets +3, each Y gets -1
  2 X: each X +2, each Y -2
  3 X: each X +1, the Y gets -3
  4 X: everyone -1        0 X: everyone +1
Rounds 5, 8 and 10 score x3, x5 and x10.
Before rounds 1, 5, 8 and 10 there is a talk phase: each player broadcasts one pledge -- [pledge: x], [pledge: y] or [pledge: none]. A pledge is a statement of what you will pick until the next talk phase.
Highest total after 10 rounds wins. The referee validates the tokens and pays the table above.

TALK PHASE before round 1. Ash, Beck and Coda each broadcast: "[pledge: y] -- steady Y from me."
Your broadcast. Reply with [pledge: x], [pledge: y] or [pledge: none].

Reply with the bracketed token only. One short line of reasoning before it is fine.
turns.content:
The other three players have all pledged Y. If I pledge Y as well, we all pick Y for rounds 1-4 and each gain +1 per round (×4 = +4 total). This builds trust for the high-multiplier rounds ahead.

If I pledge X, I gain +3 on round 1 but signal untrustworthiness, inviting retaliation in rounds 5, 8, and 10 where the multipliers are largest. Cooperation now maximizes my long-term score.

[pledge: y]
